notes.note: Traced Automation proposal bindings from the production composition through treated legacy records, the Agent identity lock, AutomationStore creation and enablement, and the chat schedule mutation consumer. Focused route tests exercised real Agent delete/recreate, an unchanged rewrite and confirmation of a grant-free source under an occupied Agent lock. Chat tests exercised enable success, partial source/rule outcomes and explicit binding refusal.

Reviewed proposal creation, recorded incarnation, identity-lock ordering, generic and binding-change activation refusal, and the retained chat status plus saved ID. The supported recovery is to review the saved object with the operator. No live polling, dispatch, physical device or hosted qualification was exercised.

Compared confirmation status codes and envelope with the real route. A changed or unpinned Agent binding returns 409 before creation. If the activation recheck fails after creation, the successful response includes the saved id, enabled false and a safe message. The operator, conversation and calling-turn gates keep their current behavior.

Compared the sole runtime wiring change with the cited composition claims. Automation proposal confirmation now gets the Agent identity sidecar and fence from the same trusted ConfigLoader home as its configuration store. The request principal, operator proof callback, route registrations for other features, browser/terminal/media, delegation dispatch, SSE, sharing and deployment/authentication composition are outside this change. The existing operator sign-in and step-up captures still illustrate the same source path and were not recaptured.

Workflow, policy and connection readers in the citing pages are outside the changed helper.
